title: Evidence of Fast Pebble Growth Near Condensation Fronts in the HL Tau Protoplanetary Disk
question: Are the dark rings (emission dips) in the ALMA HL Tau continuum images due to fast pebble growth near condensation fronts of abundant volatiles?

what.value: Best-fit inclination 46.72 deg and PA 138.02 deg

evidence.quote: using the best-fit inclination angle $i$ = 46.72$^\circ$ and PA = 138.02$^\circ$ from APR

what.value: Mid-plane temperature T_mid = 665 (r/AU)^-0.6 K from radiative transfer model of HL Tau

evidence.quote: Their best-fit model results in T$_{\rm mid}$ = 665 $(r/{\rm AU})^{-0.6}$ K for the mid-plane temperature distribution.
along with the condensation temperatures of clathrate hydrates from (cite: Lunine85) and (cite: Iro03)
$\kappa_\nu$ = 0.01 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$$(\nu/230 \rm[GHz])$ throughout the disk (cite: Ossenkopf94).

recipe.method: Shift phase center to star, deproject visibilities with inclination/PA from APR, synthesize images in each band
assumptions: Peak continuum emission marks the star; distance 140 pc

recipe.method: CLEAN nterms=2 on deprojected band 6 and 7 data

recipe.goal: Azimuthally averaged radial profiles and dip fits
recipe.method: Radial profile in 0.5 AU steps; fit smooth isothermal model; divide data by model; Gaussian fits to normalized profile give dip center, FWHM, amplitude
assumptions: kappa_nu = 0.01 cm2/g (nu/230 GHz); vertically isothermal, power-law T, Sigma of steady accretion disk

recipe.method: Compute condensation temperatures where desorption equals accretion rate, compare with brightness-temperature lower bound and MFH mid-plane temperature

recipe.goal: Dust properties with two-population opacity model
recipe.method: Examine alpha(r) in cuts at 0, 45, 90, 135 deg and azimuthal average; model alpha vs mean size of second population with mass fraction f
key_parameters: kappa_dust1 = 1 cm2/g (nu/230 GHz); rho = 1 g/cm3; f = 0.9
assumptions: Order-of-magnitude estimate; second population a >> lambda with geometric cross section

evidence.quote: The 63 AU dip is resolved at all bands, with a FWHM of 17-18 AU.

answer_key.quantity: Dip minimum relative to smooth continuum

evidence.quote: The minimum surface intensity of the dips range from 37% to 78% that of the smooth continuum from the best-fit models.

answer_key.quantity: Spectral index inside 48 AU, peaks at 13 and 32 AU dips

evidence.quote: inside of 48 AU $\alpha$$\sim$2, except for increases to values of $\sim$2.6 and $\sim$2.4 at the 13 AU and 32 AU dips, respectively

answer_key.quantity: Surface density needed for tau_1.3mm = 1 at 48 AU

evidence.quote: a surface density of $\Sigma_{\rm gas}$=100  g cm$^{-2}$  at 48 AU is needed to reach $\tau_{\rm 1.3\,mm}$ = 1

not_stated_but_needed: CLEAN parameters: weighting/robust, cell and image size, masks, threshold, scales
Whether images for radial profiles were cleaned and how the beam was matched
Best-fit isothermal model parameters (T0, q, Sigma_c, r_c, gamma) and fitting method
Radial bin averaging details and spectral index uncertainty handling
Gas number density/pressure assumptions in detail
Calibrator and flux scale details (in APR)
missing_for_reproduction: Smooth-model fit parameters and fit method
score_reason: Public data and clear outline, but imaging and fitting parameters are not given and calibrated data come from another paper.
rediscovery_reason: Public SV data, numeric dip parameters in Table 1 can be checked, though some imaging details are missing.
